verdicts.trueWording: We close out the whole section with a handy double page spread
verdicts.note: Quote appears word for word in the Sigil section, immediately before the Outlands paragraph. The closing double-page spread carries the d10 hooks, d6 faction missions, d8 calamities and a 35-entry d100 encounter table, so hooks are pooled into dice tables at the close of the Sigil section as claimed.

verdicts.trueWording: 3 pages covering 18 sites with a single paragraph each
verdicts.note: Verbatim. Full sentence opens 'The rest of the Outlands get a shorter shrift with', set against the two-page spreads the gate-towns receive, which supports the claim's 'minor'.

verdicts.trueWording: 46 pages on Sigil and 36 pages on the Outlands
verdicts.note: Verbatim, in the sentence enumerating the book's four parts (also 2 pages intro, 8 pages character options). The source calls them 'bits' rather than chapters; the two page counts match exactly.

verdicts.trueWording: Duchess Zelza Zurkbane (lawful evil succubus) and her senators
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the Ribcage section, inside a block quoted from Sigil and the Outlands and introduced as the gate-town's new ruler. Every limb present: title, given name, surname, parenthetical alignment, creature type.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the unhedged 'carry no mechanics' - the source says 'pretty much all', not all
verdicts.trueWording: No mechanics for this are offered, though
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim in the Bedlam section, where the reviewer generalises from Bedlam's mind-controlling winds to 'pretty much all of the special traits listed for these towns'. The reviewer explicitly declines the absolute, so a claim that gate-town special traits carry no mechanics overstates the source by one hedge. The substance (traits are flavour, meaning left to the DM) is otherwise supported.

verdicts.trueWording: brief blurbs, 1-2 paragraphs each, on the following
verdicts.note: Verbatim, introducing the book's 'Other Realms' list of eighteen names near the article's end. 'Minor' is the reviewer's sense too - he adds that most do not warrant much comment.

verdicts.trueWording: Descriptions are presented from the point of view of various
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the Chapter 2 gazetteer paragraph; the sentence ends 'inhabitants of the Realms'. Applies to the roughly 45 locations that chapter covers.

verdicts.trueWording: general guides to the character of a place, not an
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the same Chapter 2 paragraph; the sentence continues 'attempt at providing mechanical information or detailed maps', supporting both limbs of the claim.

verdicts.trueWording: Each location is given details that include history, potential lore
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the setting-content paragraph. History does head the list, which continues with lore, city or region maps, and firsthand accounts. Note the list is explicitly non-exhaustive ('include'), so 'first' is list order, not a claim of completeness.

verdicts.trueWording: firsthand accounts from the researchers and loremasters from whose
verdicts.note: Verbatim; the sentence closes 'perspective the book is written', which supports the claim in full.

verdicts.trueWording: has 53 pages dedicated to the city of Baldur
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the closing section, given as an example against which the reviewer measures SCAG, and paired with 24 pages for Waterdeep: Dragon Heist. The source spells the title 'Descent to Avernus'; the claim's 'Descent into Avernus' is the book's actual title.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'each' - one italic read-aloud passage carries no read-or-paraphrase instruction
verdicts.note: The quoted instruction is verbatim and recurs four times, before the departure, first-day, third-day and fourth-day passages. But the awakened dragon skull's italic speech near the end is introduced only by narration ending 'a raspy voice emerges', so the instruction is standing but not universal. The publisher limb does hold on the page as served: the footer reads (c) 2017-2024 Wizards of the Coast LLC, though the post itself dates to July 2020.
verdicts.trueWording: Read or paraphrase the following to set the scene

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the universal - one italic read-aloud passage is first-person NPC speech
verdicts.trueWording: Just past midday, you come across a smashed cart
verdicts.note: Verbatim, and the five scene-setting read-aloud passages are all second person and present tense (the departure, first day, third day and the two Bryn Shander paragraphs). The sixth italic passage, the dragon skull's line beginning 'Hey, what's the big idea', is first person, so the claim as a universal over the page's read-aloud passages has one counterexample.

verdicts.trueWording: Just past midday, you come across a smashed cart
verdicts.note: Verbatim, and the italic passage is exactly two sentences: the smashed cart at the roadside, then two sets of tracks leading into a fir grove. The next paragraph is DM-facing, so the passage does close there. The heading reads 'On the First Day, an Exploration Encounter: Following the Tracks'.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'each' - most DM-facing paragraphs carry no run-in label
verdicts.trueWording: Investigating the Cart. This cart is a simple wooden carriage
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim, and the 'bolded' limb holds: the label is marked up bold and italic together (strong wrapping em), as are Following the Tracks, End of the Line, Terrain and Tactics, Wrath and Retreat, Treasure, Speaking with Ogden, Raggamel the Renegade and Delivering to Raggamel. But twelve labelled paragraphs sit against roughly twenty-eight unlabelled DM-facing prose paragraphs, so the labels mark sub-topics within an encounter rather than opening every DM-facing paragraph.
